title: Speculative mix scheduler with per-request accuracy probes
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: We need a low-latency strategy for choosing execution paths across FP16/FP8/INT8 that minimizes customer-visible regression while improving unit cost. Existing calibration-driven routing is conservative and causes missed cost savings on tail requests with short sequences. Goal: implement a speculative mix scheduler that can route a small fraction of requests to lower-precision kernels with an inline accuracy probe and shadow validation. The scheduler should be per-request (not only per-model) and support fast rollback/fallback when probe signals drift.

Scope: implement runtime scheduling + lightweight per-request probe, shadow execution harness for periodic validation, new telemetry events, and rollout plan (canary + rollout gating). This ticket covers design, runtime implementation, test coverage, and an initial canary. Subsequent tickets will expand coverage and model-specific profiles.

Non-goals: full model re-calibration pipeline, exhaustive offline quantization tooling (handled by quant-team), or UI changes in Console (except basic telemetry links).

Design sketch: The scheduler is speculatively optimistic: by default it executes on FP16, but for X% of requests (configurable per-route) it attempts a cheaper execution path (INT8/FP8) with two probes appended: 1) a fast lightweight accuracy heuristic run inline that compares logits/entropy signature against a local threshold; 2) an async shadow validator that replays the request on the golden path and computes a strict L2/logit-diff metric. If inline probe passes, response is returned immediately from cheap path. If probe fails or async shadow reports regression above threshold, that route is temporarily suspended for the route+model for a cooldown period.

Key decisions and tradeoffs: 
- Inline probe must be cheaper than golden execution; we use a top-k logit sketch and entropy delta rather than full softmax. This trades some probe fidelity for latency.
- Async shadow validation provides higher-fidelity accuracy checks but is eventually consistent — rollback is based on aggregate stats and not per-request.
- Sampling rate defaults to 1% per-route to minimize risk; we expose per-route config and a global kill-switch.
- Safety: any request containing "safety_sensitive=true" metadata bypasses speculative routing.

Telemetry and metrics: per-route probes_sent, probes_passed_inline, shadow_mismatch_rate, avg_latency_fp16, avg_latency_int8, rollback_events, cooling_period_active. Add tracing hooks in request flow to correlate probe outcomes with SDK request IDs.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative scheduler implemented in runtime with pluggable precision backends (FP16/FP8/INT8)
Inline probe computed within < 1ms median overhead for 8k context on p4d-equivalent hardware
Async shadow validator computes logit L2 difference and reports mismatch rate per-route to telemetry (visible in metrics platform)
Route-level configuration exists and supports sampling_rate, quick_kill boolean, cooldown_seconds
Rollout plan executed: canary at 1% traffic for two model families without customer visible regressions; rollback mechanism exercised in tests
Unit and integration tests cover probe failures, rollback state machine, and cold-start behavior
